title: IndiGo Signs Record Deal for Over 1,000 CFM LEAP Engines to Power Its Expanding Airbus Fleet
excerpt: India’s largest airline locked in a memorandum of understanding with CFM International for the biggest single engine order in the manufacturer’s history.
body:
• IndiGo signed an MoU with CFM International for over 1,000 LEAP-1A engines, the largest single order in CFM’s history
  • CFM International, co-owned by GE Aerospace and France’s Safran, is the world’s largest engine maker by units sold
  • The deal deepens IndiGo’s shift away from Pratt and Whitney’s geared turbofan engines following years of maintenance disruptions
  • India’s aviation sector is poised for explosive growth, with IndiGo adding one aircraft per week as part of a broader fleet overhaul

IndiGo, India’s largest airline by passengers and fleet size, has signed a memorandum of understanding with CFM International for over 1,000 LEAP-1A engines — the biggest single order in the engine maker’s history, Reuters reported on Monday.

The Scale of the Deal

CFM International, a 50-50 joint venture between GE Aerospace and France’s Safran, makes engines for the Boeing 737 MAX and competes with Pratt and Whitney on the Airbus A320neo family. It is the world’s largest engine maker by number of units sold.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=2XIxAbgnR0Y

While financial terms were not disclosed, the deal’s scale dwarfs IndiGo’s previous engine agreements. In 2019, the airline selected LEAP-1A engines for 280 A320neo family aircraft in a deal valued at approximately $20 billion. A subsequent order covered another 310 aircraft with 620 engines. This latest MoU for over 1,000 engines suggests a deal worth well in excess of $30 billion at list prices, though airlines of IndiGo’s size routinely negotiate steep discounts.

Why CFM Over Pratt and Whitney

The order represents a decisive consolidation of IndiGo’s engine strategy around CFM. The airline’s earlier A320neo fleet relied on Pratt and Whitney’s geared turbofan engines, which suffered from persistent maintenance problems that grounded aircraft and disrupted operations. India’s aviation regulator at one point ordered the replacement of all earlier-generation Pratt and Whitney engines on A320neo aircraft as a safety precaution.

https://x.com/IndiGo6E/status/2079232522278650260

IndiGo has maintained that its shift to CFM was driven by commercial considerations, but the GTF reliability issues clearly accelerated the transition. The LEAP engine, which has logged over 10 million flight hours in commercial service, offers 15% lower fuel consumption and CO2 emissions compared to its predecessor, the CFM56.

India’s Aviation Boom

The engine deal reflects the staggering pace of India’s aviation expansion. IndiGo currently adds roughly one aircraft per week as part of the broader fleet transformation underway across Indian carriers. The Air India Group is similarly scaling up, having placed orders for hundreds of new aircraft as part of a massive fleet modernization programme.

India is on track to become the world’s third-largest aviation market by passengers within the decade, driven by a growing middle class, increasing urbanization, and improving airport infrastructure.

"This is a pivotal milestone that reflects our long-standing commitment to rapidly strengthen our network both domestically and internationally."

— Ronojoy Dutta, former IndiGo CEO, on an earlier CFM deal

What’s Next

The MoU is not a binding contract — final terms, delivery schedules, and the associated long-term service agreements will need to be negotiated before the order is confirmed. But the sheer volume signals IndiGo’s confidence in sustained demand for air travel in India and its intent to dominate not just domestically but on international routes, where its A321XLR aircraft will open new long-haul possibilities.

For travellers, particularly in the Indian diaspora, IndiGo’s aggressive fleet expansion translates directly into more routes, higher frequency, and competitive fares on connections between India and the world.
